concepts.name: Wavefunction amplitude
concepts.explanation: An orbital is a one-electron spatial wavefunction. Its amplitude may be signed or complex; it is not a probability or a charge. A CUBE stores a scalar field, so its generating calculation must identify whether it contains an orbital, density or another quantity.

concepts.name: Probability density
concepts.explanation: For a normalized one-electron wavefunction, |ψ(r)|² is nonnegative and integrates to one. Probability in a region is its volume integral. The square of one molecular orbital is not the total many-electron density. These synthetic CUBE values have no demonstrated physical normalization.

concepts.name: Orbital phase
concepts.explanation: For a real orbital, opposite signs represent phases differing by π. Reversing the entire sign changes neither |ψ|² nor any observable. Relative phases within a superposition affect interference. Positive/negative colors never mean positive/negative electric charge.

concepts.name: Electron density
concepts.explanation: The electron number density n(r) integrates to the electron count. In a natural-orbital representation it is an occupation-weighted sum Σᵢ nᵢ|φᵢ(r)|²; a general orbital basis uses the one-particle density matrix. Electronic charge density is −e times this number density.

concepts.name: Excitation energy
concepts.explanation: An excitation energy is the difference between many-electron electronic-state energies. Photon wavelength is hc/ΔE. A vertical electronic excitation holds the nuclear geometry fixed. It is not generally equal to a ground-state HOMO–LUMO orbital-energy difference.

concepts.name: Oscillator strength
concepts.explanation: The dimensionless oscillator strength quantifies transition intensity. In the electric-dipole approximation it depends on excitation energy and the squared transition dipole matrix element. It is neither an orbital occupation, an NTO weight, nor a fluorescence quantum yield.

concepts.name: Absorption spectrum
concepts.explanation: A transition table supplies discrete sticks. An assumed lineshape turns them into an envelope. Here each Gaussian has area f in energy space; width changes height and overlap. The wavelength view retains f/eV, so integrating it over nm does not yield total oscillator strength. No experimental absorbance is computed.

concepts.name: HOMO/LUMO terminology
concepts.explanation: HOMO and LUMO identify the highest occupied and lowest unoccupied orbitals of a stated reference and spin convention. A transition can contain multiple occupied-to-virtual contributions. Assigning one needs state-resolved coefficients, occupation/index metadata and the corresponding orbital files.

concepts.name: NTO hole/electron orbitals
concepts.explanation: Natural transition orbitals give paired hole and electron channels for a particular electronic transition, with weights from the transition-density analysis. They are not automatically the HOMO and LUMO. Keep state, pair, spin, weight convention and exported CUBE mapping together. No such pair or weight is supplied here.

missing_data.artifact: Matched molecule/geometry identity, charge, multiplicity, reference state, method, basis, solvent/environment, program/version and calculation convergence; original input/output hashes tying every artifact to the same job.

Full state-resolved excitation output with state IDs, energies, oscillator strengths, transition dipoles and occupied-to-virtual contributions (coefficients and their method-specific interpretation), spin labels and printing threshold.

CUBEs of the contributing orbitals with field type, orbital index, zero/one-based convention, occupations, geometry/grid units and a mapping to the state contributions. One unsigned label or filename is insufficient.

State-specific NTO hole/electron CUBE pairs plus printed pair weights, normalization/threshold convention, spin and source wavefunction/transition-density provenance. Optional for an MO-based assignment; mandatory for an NTO claim.

missing_data.required_for: Comparison with experiment or hardware use
missing_data.artifact: Measured absorption with sample identity, concentration/path length, solvent/temperature, calibration and uncertainty, plus the application-specific response model. This is separate from a defensible computed transition assignment.

manual_handoffs: Requester → computational chemist: provide molecule, geometry, charge/spin and the spectral question; select an appropriate electronic-structure method and environmental model.
Computational chemist → artifact producer: review convergence and state composition; export corresponding orbital CUBEs, and NTO pairs/weights when relevant, using the producing engine.

Artifact producer → Orbital Studio operator: supply a hashed job manifest with field types, units, orbital/state indices and pair mapping; preserve the original calculation output alongside any CSV fallback.

Orbital Studio operator → scientific reviewer: inspect fields, table and broadened exports; reconcile indexing and geometry; separate observed values, derived conversions and assumed display settings.

Scientific reviewer → CAID/educator: approve only supported transition statements; attach evidence and unresolved questions. Experimental/material qualification and any validated CAID import are subsequent work.
